sentences.text:
11 September, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Venkateswarlu Nimmagadda
 Writ Petition No.12842 of 2020
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"to issue a writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of respondents in seeking to lay the road through the lands of the petitioners situated in Sy.No.5-1 in Sultanagaram, Gollapalem Village of Machilipatnam Mandal, Krishna District without following due course of law as wholly illegal, arbitrary and in violation of Articles 14, 21 and 300A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents not lay the road through the land of the petitioners situated in Sy.No.5-1 in Sultanagaram, Gollapalem Village of Machilipatnam Mandal, Krishna District and to pass such other order or orders ....."

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Government Pleader for Revenue.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners herein are the absolute owners and possessors of the agricultural land in Sy.No.5-1 situated in Sultanagaram, Gollapalem Village of Machilipatnam Mandal, Krishna District.

While that being so, Respondent Nos.3 to 5 are taking steps and proposing to lay the clay road under NREGS Programme through the petitioners lands without initiating any procedure either under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No. 30 of 2013) or under any law enacted by Respondent No.1.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act No. 30 of 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence, Respondent Nos.3 to 5 cannot be interfered without following the due process of law, which is in violation of Articles 14, 21 and 300A of the Constitution of India.

4. On the other hand, learned Government Pleader for Revenue submits that in view of the interim orders passed by this Court on 30.07.2020, the respondents are not interfering with the petitioners'
subject property.
He further submits that if any such proposal is made, the respondents will follow the due process of law as contemplated under the Act.

5. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the parties, it is settled principle of law, if the respondents intend to lay any road through the petitioners property they are under the statutory obligation to follow due procedure of law as contemplated under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (No. 30 of 2013).
